newsitem.title: UK: EIB to launch 1.0 trillion lire-into-euro Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: EIB to launch 1.0 trillion lire-into-euro Eurobond.

text.p: The European Investment Bank will launch a 1.0 trillion lire Eurobond next week, syndicate sources said on Friday.

The deal, which will carry a 5.75 percent coupon and mature on February 15, 2007, will be redenominated in euros after EMU and then be fungible with other EIB deals denominated in escudos, French francs, guilders and marks which were launched earlier this year.
Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, Credito Italiano and Paribas will be joint lead managers.

Rene Karsenti, director general of finance at the European Investment Bank, told bankers at a conference here earlier this week it would launch more "euro-tributary transactions. We have launched deals in four (EMU) currencies so far this year. There will be more."

Euro-tributary deals, or parallel bonds, are bonds launched in more than one currency but with the same coupon and maturity date. They contain clauses which allow for their redenomination into euros after EMU and ensuing fungibility.

The third stage of European economic and monetary union, including the introduction of the European Union's planned single currency, the euro, is prescribed by EU law to take place no later than January 1, 1999.
